Fatal and non-fatal pancreatitis has been observed in patients undergoing therapy with didanosine (VIDEX), whether used alone or in combination with other drugs, in both treatment-naïve and treatment-experienced patients, regardless of their level of immunosuppression. 2. Didanosine should be immediately suspended in patients presenting with signs or symptoms of pancreatitis and permanently discontinued in those with confirmed pancreatitis. 3. Patients receiving didanosine in combination with stavudine may have an increased risk of developing pancreatitis. 4. If treatment with life-sustaining drugs known to cause pancreatic toxicity is necessary, it is recommended to suspend didanosine therapy. 5. In patients with risk factors for pancreatitis, didanosine should be used with extreme caution and only if clearly indicated. 6. Patients with advanced HIV-1 infection, particularly elderly individuals, are at a heightened risk of pancreatitis and should be closely monitored. 7. Patients with renal impairment may face an increased risk of pancreatitis if treated with didanosine without appropriate dose adjustments. 8. The frequency of pancreatitis is dose-dependent. 9. Lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis, including fatal cases, have been reported with the use of nucleoside analogues, including didanosine, either alone or in combination with other antiretrovirals. 10. Most cases of lactic acidosis and hepatomegaly with steatosis have occurred in women. 11. Risk factors for these conditions may include obesity and prolonged exposure to nucleoside analogues. 12. Fatal lactic acidosis has been reported in pregnant women receiving a combination of didanosine and stavudine with other antiretroviral agents. 13. The combination of didanosine and stavudine should be used with caution during pregnancy and only if the potential benefits clearly outweigh the risks. 14. Special caution is advised when administering didanosine to patients with known risk factors for liver disease, although cases have also been reported in patients without such risk factors. 15. Didanosine therapy should be suspended in any patient who develops clinical signs or symptoms consistent with symptomatic hyperlactatemia, lactic acidosis, or significant hepatotoxicity, even in the absence of marked transaminase elevations. 16. The safety and efficacy of didanosine have not been established in HIV-infected patients with significant underlying liver disease. 17. Patients with preexisting liver dysfunction, including chronic active hepatitis, may experience an increased frequency of liver function abnormalities, including severe and potentially fatal hepatic adverse events, during combination antiretroviral therapy. These patients should be monitored according to standard clinical practice. 18. If there is evidence of worsening liver disease in such patients, interruption or discontinuation of treatment must be considered. 19. Hepatotoxicity and hepatic failure resulting in death have been reported during postmarketing surveillance in HIV-infected patients treated with hydroxyurea and other antiretroviral agents. 20. Fatal hepatic events were most frequently reported in patients treated with the combination of hydroxyurea, didanosine, and stavudine. This combination should be avoided. 21. Cases of non-cirrhotic portal hypertension have been reported postmarketing, including cases leading to liver transplantation or death. 22. Didanosine-associated non-cirrhotic portal hypertension has been confirmed by liver biopsy in patients without evidence of viral hepatitis. 23. The onset of signs and symptoms of non-cirrhotic portal hypertension ranged from months to years after initiating didanosine therapy. 24. Common presenting features include elevated liver enzymes, esophageal varices, hematemesis, ascites, and splenomegaly. 25. Patients receiving didanosine should be monitored for early signs of portal hypertension, such as thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly, during routine medical visits. 26. Appropriate laboratory testing, including liver enzymes, serum bilirubin, albumin, complete blood count, international normalized ratio (INR), and ultrasonography, should be considered. 27. Didanosine should be discontinued in patients with evidence of non-cirrhotic portal hypertension. 28. Peripheral neuropathy, characterized by numbness, tingling, or pain in the hands or feet, has been reported in patients receiving didanosine therapy. 29. Peripheral neuropathy occurs more frequently in patients with advanced HIV disease, a history of neuropathy, or those receiving neurotoxic drug therapy, including stavudine. 30. Discontinuation of didanosine should be considered in patients who develop peripheral neuropathy. 31. Retinal changes and optic neuritis have been reported in both adult and pediatric patients receiving didanosine. 32. Periodic retinal examinations should be considered for patients undergoing didanosine therapy. 33. Immune reconstitution syndrome has been reported in patients treated with combination antiretroviral therapy, including didanosine. 34. During the initial phase of combination antiretroviral treatment, patients with immune system recovery may develop an inflammatory response to indolent or residual opportunistic infections, such as Mycobacterium avium infection, cytomegalovirus, Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia, or tuberculosis, which may require further evaluation and treatment. 35. Autoimmune disorders, such as Graves’ disease, polymyositis, and Guillain-Barré syndrome, have also been reported in the context of immune reconstitution. However, the onset of these conditions is more variable and can occur many months after initiating treatment. 36. Redistribution or accumulation of body fat, including central obesity, dorsocervical fat enlargement (buffalo hump), peripheral wasting, facial wasting, breast enlargement, and a cushingoid appearance, has been observed in patients receiving antiretroviral therapy. 37. The mechanism and long-term consequences of these events are currently unknown. 38. A causal relationship between antiretroviral therapy and fat redistribution has not been established.
